method: Twenty-four existing public practice positions, three per group. Three explanations use cached Stockfish research lines whose generator checked a minimum depth of 20; twenty-one use published previews of up to six plies with no exported engine version, achieved depth, or absolute score. Board claims and all saved moves are checked by legal replay. These are explanations of specific continuations, not proofs that all replies are forced or complete explanations of evaluation differences. The terminal checkmate explicitly identified in one saved line is checked on the board. No new engine searches or private mining candidates are used.

items.title: Clear f4 for the king
items.constraint: White’s pawn on g3 guards f4, keeping the black king out of that square.
items.purpose: The pawn push ...f4 offers a way to remove that guard: after gxf4, Black can approach the pawn with ...Kf5.
items.continuation: The saved line goes ...f4 gxf4 ...Kf5 Bf1 ...Kxf4. Black’s king reaches f4 and protects the pawn on e4.
items.notice: Watch the g3-pawn leave its square, then follow the king from f6 to f5 to f4.

evidence.depth_kind: verified minimum; exact achieved depth was not exported

comparison.depth_kind: verified minimum; exact achieved depth was not exported
comparison.explanation: After the immediate ...Ke5, the cached line is f4+ exf3 en passant Bxf3. Black’s e4-pawn disappears, while White’s g3-pawn still guards f4.

items.title: Turn the bishop toward c4
items.constraint: White’s bishop sits on c4. Black’s bishop on f5 does not yet attack it.
items.purpose: ...Be6 points the bishop down the e6–d5–c4 diagonal. Black’s queen on f6 protects the bishop on its new square.
items.continuation: In the saved line, f3 is met by ...Bxc4. Then Qxe4 Qxb2 trades Black’s e4-pawn for White’s b2-pawn after the bishop capture.
items.notice: Trace the bishop’s new diagonal to c4 and the queen’s protection along the sixth rank.

items.title: Line up the queen and rook
items.constraint: White’s queen on e3 stands in front of the rook on c1 on the h6–c1 diagonal.
items.purpose: ...Bh6 attacks the queen. If that diagonal clears, the bishop can reach the rook behind it.
items.continuation: White first counters with Nd5, attacking Black’s queen. After ...Qg7 Qd3, the line continues ...Bxc1 Rxc1: Black exchanges a bishop for a rook.
items.notice: Look behind the attacked queen before deciding where it should move.

items.title: Use both knights against f2
items.constraint: White’s king is still on e1. Black’s knight on d4 blocks the bishop on b6 from looking all the way to f2.
items.purpose: ...Ng4 attacks f2. In the saved line, one knight draws the king onto f2, and the other clears the bishop’s diagonal with check.
items.continuation: After h3 Nxf2 Kxf2, ...Nxf3+ captures White’s knight and uncovers the bishop’s check from b6. White blocks with Be3. The king has left e1 and can no longer castle.
items.notice: The check after ...Nxf3+ comes from the bishop on b6, not the knight on f3.

evidence.depth_kind: verified minimum; exact achieved depth was not exported

comparison.depth_kind: verified minimum; exact achieved depth was not exported
comparison.explanation: With ...Bg4 instead, the cached line begins Be2 Nxe2 Qxe2. Black trades the d4-knight on e2, and White’s king remains on e1 rather than being drawn to f2.

items.title: Check before taking g6
items.constraint: White has an advanced pawn on g6 and a king on e1, with no piece between the king and e8 on the e-file.
items.purpose: ...Qe8+ makes White answer a check and places the queen on the e8–f7–g6 diagonal.
items.continuation: The saved reply is Kf2. Black then takes the pawn with ...Qxg6; after Kg1, ...Rae8 brings the a8-rook onto the e-file.
items.notice: Follow the queen from f8 to e8 to g6: the first move is a check, the second a capture.

items.title: Pin the pawn that attacks the queen
items.constraint: White’s pawn on g3 attacks Black’s queen on h4.
items.purpose: ...Rg5 pins that pawn to the king on g1. Taking the queen with gxh4 would expose the king to the rook, so that capture is illegal.
items.continuation: In the saved line, Kh1 removes the pin by leaving the g-file. Black then moves the queen with ...Qh3; Rg1 is met by ...Qh5.
items.notice: Both cached evaluations still favour White. The pin is a defensive resource, not a forced win.

evidence.depth_kind: verified minimum; exact achieved depth was not exported

comparison.depth_kind: verified minimum; exact achieved depth was not exported
comparison.explanation: After the immediate ...Qh3, the cached line continues Qd2 h5 Rd8. White gets a rook to the eighth rank; ...Rff8 Rxe8 Rxe8 follows. The saved score is worse for Black than after ...Rg5.

items.title: Back up the f7 rook
items.constraint: White’s bishop on b3 attacks the rook on f7, while the white pawn on d6 is close to promotion.
items.purpose: After ...Qe8, the queen can recapture on f7 while the king stays on g8.
items.continuation: The saved line is Qxa7 h6 Bxf7+ Qxf7 d7. White exchanges the bishop for Black’s rook; Black’s queen takes over on f7, but White’s passed pawn reaches d7.
items.notice: After the exchange on f7, look at White’s pawn on d7.

items.title: Support the queen’s entry on g2
items.constraint: The pawn on g2 sits beside White’s king on g1.
items.purpose: ...Bf3 guards g2, supporting a queen capture next to the king.
items.continuation: In the saved line, Kf1 is met by ...Qxg2+. White cannot take that queen with the king because the bishop protects it. After Ke1, ...Qxb2 takes White’s bishop.
items.notice: Before following the queen, check which piece protects its landing square.

items.title: Fork the queen and rook
items.constraint: White’s queen is on g3 and the rook is on e1. From c3, Black’s queen can attack both.
items.purpose: ...Qc3 creates the fork. The bishop on g7 protects the queen along the g7–f6–e5–d4–c3 diagonal.
items.continuation: White answers with Qe3 in the saved line. After ...Qxe3 Rxe3, the queens are exchanged and White’s rook has moved from e1 to e3.
items.notice: From c3, look across the third rank toward the queen and diagonally toward the rook.

items.title: Put the bishop on the queen’s diagonal
items.constraint: White’s queen on b7 is attacking the rook on a8.
items.purpose: ...Be4 attacks that queen along e4–d5–c6–b7. It also puts the bishop on a line to a8 if White takes the rook.
items.continuation: The saved reply is Qxa8. Black answers ...Bxa8; after Rxd8+, ...Qxd8 captures White’s rook on d8. This is the consequence of the rook capture shown in the line.
items.notice: Follow the bishop’s diagonal all the way to a8 before taking that rook.

items.title: Remove the pawn blocking b4
items.constraint: White’s pawn on b3 blocks Black’s pawn on b4.
items.purpose: ...a4 attacks the blocker from the side. If Black captures on b3, the a-pawn can continue down the b-file.
items.continuation: The saved line is ...a4 Qd3 ...axb3 Re1 ...b2. Black’s pawn reaches b2, where the queen on a3 protects it.
items.notice: Track the a-pawn’s route: a5–a4–b3–b2.

items.title: Draw one rook away from the other
items.constraint: White’s rook on a2 protects the rook on a8 along the a-file.
items.purpose: ...Rxc2+ gives check with the c7-rook. In the saved reply, Rxc2 draws White’s lower rook off the a-file, leaving the a8-rook for Black’s other rook.
items.continuation: After ...Rxc2+ Rxc2, Black plays ...Rxa8 with the rook from c8. One black rook draws the defender away; the other makes the capture.
items.notice: Watch which rook moves each time. The two black rooks have different jobs.

items.title: Draw the king onto a diagonal
items.constraint: White’s king is on b2, beside its pawn on a3.
items.purpose: ...Bxa3+ offers the bishop with check. After the king takes on a3, ...Qe7+ reaches it along the e7–d6–c5–b4–a3 diagonal.
items.continuation: The saved line continues Kxa3 Qe7+ Kb2 Qb4+ Kc1. The bishop sacrifice opens a sequence of queen checks against the exposed king.
items.notice: At each queen check, trace the open line from the queen to the king.

items.title: Fork two pieces and open the g-file
items.constraint: White’s queen on d3 and rook on e2 are both within reach of a knight on f4.
items.purpose: ...Nf4 attacks both pieces. White can take the knight with gxf4, but that moves the g3-pawn off the g-file.
items.continuation: In the saved line, gxf4 is followed by ...Bxc4 Qxc4. Black then plays ...Qg4+, checking down the newly opened g-file, and White replies Kf1.
items.notice: Compare the g-file before gxf4 and after it. The pawn’s old square matters to the queen’s check.

items.title: Take the checking capture first
items.constraint: White has knights on c3 and f7. Black’s bishop on b4 can capture the first with check, while the rook on f8 attacks the second.
items.purpose: ...Bxc3+ starts with the checking capture. After bxc3, Black follows with ...Rxf7; the saved continuation then exchanges the rook for White’s bishop as well.
items.continuation: The line is ...Bxc3+ bxc3 ...Rxf7 Bxf7+ ...Kxf7 O-O. Black has exchanged a bishop and rook for two knights and a bishop; White then castles.
items.notice: Count the captured pieces across the whole sequence, rather than stopping at the rook capture on f7.

items.title: Clear both blockers on the long diagonal
items.constraint: Black’s knight on f6 and White’s knight on c3 stand between the bishop on g7 and White’s bishop on b2.
items.purpose: ...Nfxe4 clears f6 and takes a pawn. In the saved reply, Nxe4 also pulls White’s c3-knight off that diagonal, allowing ...Bxb2.
items.continuation: After ...Nfxe4 Nxe4 ...Bxb2, White captures the other knight with Nxc5. Black’s rook recaptures with ...Rxc5.
items.notice: The bishop needs two squares cleared: f6 by Black’s move, then c3 by White’s reply.

items.title: Use the rook behind the queen
items.constraint: White’s pawn on h2 sits directly in front of the king on h1. Black’s queen and rook share the h-file.
items.purpose: ...Qxh2+ takes the pawn with check. After Nxh2, the knight is on a square the h8-rook can capture; Black’s knight on f3 also guards h2.
items.continuation: The saved line is ...Qxh2+ Nxh2 ...Rxh2#. The rook’s recapture is checkmate in this position.
items.notice: Look past the queen to the rook behind it, and check how the knight on f3 supports h2.

items.title: Open the bishop’s diagonal with check
items.constraint: Black’s knight on e4 blocks the bishop on g6 from attacking White’s bishop on c2.
items.purpose: ...Ng3+ clears that diagonal while checking the king on f1. The knight also attacks the rook on h1.
items.continuation: White takes the knight with fxg3 in the saved line. Black then plays ...Bxc2, capturing the bishop that the knight had been blocking from view.
items.notice: Follow two attacks after ...Ng3+: the knight’s check and the bishop’s new line to c2.

items.title: Clear the e-file for the rook
items.constraint: Black’s bishop on e2 blocks the e7-rook’s route to e1.
items.purpose: ...Bh5 clears the file. In the saved line, the rook can then enter on e1, where Black’s queen on g3 protects it.
items.continuation: After ...Bh5 Rf1 ...Re1 Rf4, Black plays ...Rxf1+ and White answers Rxf1. The file clearance leads to a rook exchange on the first rank.
items.notice: Watch e2 become empty, then trace the rook’s route from e7 to e1 to f1.

items.title: Fork the queen and rook with a pawn
items.constraint: White’s queen on d4 and rook on b4 sit on the two capture squares of a black pawn on c5.
items.purpose: ...c5 attacks both major pieces at once.
items.continuation: White answers with Qg4+ in the saved line. Black takes with ...Qxg4, and Rxg4+ exchanges the queens while leaving White’s rook on g4.
items.notice: Notice White’s checking reply before assuming the pawn fork simply wins the rook.

items.title: Attack the queen and clear the seventh rank
items.constraint: Black’s bishop on d7 stands between the queen on e7 and White’s bishop on c7.
items.purpose: ...Ba4 attacks White’s queen on c2 and clears d7, opening Black’s queen’s route to c7.
items.continuation: In the saved line, White takes the bishop with Qxa4. Black replies ...Qxc7, trading bishops after moving the white queen away from c2.
items.notice: The bishop’s move changes two lines: a4–b3–c2 and e7–d7–c7.

items.title: Bring the queen onto the bishop’s diagonal
items.constraint: White’s queen on f3 protects the pawn on f2, beside the king on g1.
items.purpose: After ...Rxf2 Qxf2, ...Bd4 pins the queen to the king along d4–e3–f2–g1. Black’s queen on c5 protects the bishop.
items.continuation: White chooses Rf1 in the saved line. Black then takes the queen with ...Bxf2+, and Raxf2 recaptures the bishop.
items.notice: Line up d4, e3, f2 and g1: the queen stands between the bishop and the king.

items.title: Draw the rook off the back rank
items.constraint: White’s rook on d1 blocks the line from a1 to the king on e1.
items.purpose: ...Rxd2 offers Black’s rook for the knight. The saved reply Rxd2 pulls White’s rook off d1, allowing ...Qa1+ along the back rank.
items.continuation: After ...Rxd2 Rxd2 ...Qa1+, White returns the rook to d1. Black then changes direction with ...Qc3+, checking along c3–d2–e1; White replies Ke2.
items.notice: Follow the rook as it leaves d1 and returns, then trace the queen’s second check.

items.title: Use two checks to take both bishops
items.constraint: White has bishops on g2 and d2, with the king between them on f2.
items.purpose: ...Rxg2+ captures one bishop with check. After Kxg2, ...Re2+ brings Black’s other rook to the second rank with another check.
items.continuation: The saved line continues Kf3 Rxd2. Across the sequence, Black gives up the g8-rook for both bishops and keeps the other rook on d2.
items.notice: Track the two rooks separately: the first takes on g2, the second enters on e2 and takes on d2.
